newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sells 7.29 bln reais in Treasury debt.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sells 7.29 bln reais in Treasury debt.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank, on behalf of the National Treasury, raised 7.29 billion reais during an auction of Treasury Notes and Letters, dealers said.
A total of 4.23 billion reais was sold in two series of National Treasury Letters known as LTNs.
A total of 3.42 billion reais of 181-day LTNs, due May 1, 1997, was sold at an overnight call money rate of 2.60 percent a month.
The Central Bank also sold 815.4 million reais of 365-day LTNs, due in November 1 1997, at a call money rate of 2.44 percent a month.
Some 2.35 billion reais were sold in National Treasury Notes (NTN) indexed to the variation of Brazil's reference rate (TR).
The notes, which are due May 1, 1997, pay annual yields of 12.82 percent plus the variation of the TR in the maturity period.

The Central Bank sold a series of NTNs indexed to the variation of the dollar, known as NTN-D. A total of 708.7 million reais in NTN-D with a maturity period of two years will pay annual yields of 12.90 percent, dealers said.
